BiblicalUsage: Sarat is gashing the flesh, and the law forbids it: the priests shall not make any cuttings in their flesh. Zechariah uses the same word for a different cutting — all that burden themselves with Jerusalem shall be cut in pieces.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that God forbids His people to wound themselves in grief, because their bodies belong to Him and their mourning is not to look like the pagans'.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
